text: Supports a Brewfile that encodes a project's dependencies like package.json or Gemfile, enabling one-command environment bootstrap
quote: Adding a `Brewfile` to a project's repository (like you might a `package.json`, `Gemfile` or `requirements.txt`) is a nicer way of encoding project dependencies for developer environments.

text: brew bundle dump snapshots installed formulae, casks, taps and other package types into a Brewfile
quote: `brew bundle dump` is Homebrew's installed-state snapshot command: it records supported installed formulae, casks, taps and other package types as a `Brewfile`.

text: Bundler supports non-Ruby dependency types: Homebrew formulae, casks, Mac App Store, VSCode extensions, Go, Cargo, uv, Flatpak, WinGet, Krew and npm packages
quote: Bundler for non-Ruby dependencies from Homebrew formulae, Homebrew casks, Mac App Store dependencies, VSCode (and forks/variants) extensions, Go packages, Cargo packages, uv tools, Flatpak packages, WinGet packages, Krew plugins and npm pac

text: brew create can scaffold a new formula definition directly from a source tarball URL
quote:
$ brew create https://ffmpeg.org/releases/ffmpeg-8.1.1.tar.xz
Created .../homebrew-core/Formula/ffmpeg.rb

text: brew tap lets users add third-party repositories providing extra formulae, casks and external commands, and brew untap removes them
quote: The `brew tap` command adds repositories that Homebrew can use for formulae, casks and external commands.

text: No sudo is required for brew install after the initial Homebrew setup
quote: you don't need _sudo_ after Homebrew's initial installation when you `brew install`

text: brew autoremove uninstalls formulae that were only installed as dependencies and are no longer needed
quote: Uninstall formulae that were only installed as a dependency of another formula and are now no longer needed.

text: Prebuilt binary bottles matching the user's system are downloaded and installed automatically instead of compiling from source
quote: When the formula being installed defines a bottle matching your system, it will be downloaded and installed automatically when you run `brew install <formula>`.

text: Users can control and disable Homebrew's anonymous aggregate usage analytics
quote: Control Homebrew's anonymous aggregate user behaviour analytics.

text: Supports MDM/Munki/Jamf workflows where brew runs as root but performs operations as the logged-in console user
quote: This is intended for MDM, Munki and Jamf workflows where `brew` is invoked as root but Homebrew operations should run as the logged-in console user.

text: Lets users install newer software versions than what's available on an old host Linux distribution
quote: Install up-to-date versions of software when your host distribution is old

text: Same package manager works across macOS, Linux and Windows (WSL)
quote: Use the same package manager to manage your macOS, Linux and Windows systems

text: brew bundle check verifies whether a Brewfile's dependencies are already satisfied before running an install
quote:
You can check if a `brew bundle install` will do anything by running:


$ brew bundle check

text: Can restrict trust to a single fully-qualified formula or tap when installing
quote: Install a fully qualified item to trust only that item:

text: --bottle-arch flag lets users override bottle architecture only when reviewed for compatibility
quote: Use `--bottle-arch=` only when the formula intentionally requires another architecture and its compatibility has been reviewed.

text: Casks install upstream pre-built binaries such as applications, fonts and plugins
quote: Casks are package definitions that install upstream pre-built binaries such as applications, fonts and plugins.

text: Provides a .pkg installer for interactive or unattended MDM deployment
quote: try our `.pkg` installer for interactive or unattended MDM installs

text: Can install software not packaged for the user's Linux distribution without requiring sudo
quote: It can also install software not packaged for your Linux distribution without requiring `sudo`.

text: Installs each package into its own isolated keg in the Cellar and symlinks its files into the shared prefix
quote: It installs each package into its own keg inside the Cellar, then symlinks its files into the prefix

text: brew create --cask scaffolds a new cask definition directly from a downloadable installer URL
quote: $ brew create --cask https://download-installer.cdn.mozilla.net/pub/firefox/releases/151.0.3/mac/en-US/Firefox%20151.0.3.dmg

text: Running brew bundle install reads the Brewfile and installs any missing declared packages (e.g. brew install ruby)
quote: this will take instructions from the Brewfile to run brew install ruby and install Ruby if needed

text: brew bundle exec runs a shell session with the environment set up according to the Brewfile
quote: Run your shell in a `brew bundle exec` environment.

text: Supports strict security auditing of an installed package via brew audit --strict
quote: perform a strict audit on a package you use e.g. `brew audit --strict ffmpeg` for FFmpeg

text: Supports fully non-interactive installation by prepending NONINTERACTIVE=1 to the install command
quote: prepend `NONINTERACTIVE=1` to the installation command
